html:
A huge rock-fill dam on the Euphrates river in southeastern Turkey, built from 1983 to 1990 and named after Mustafa Kemal Atatürk. It is the largest dam on the river.

It is the centrepiece of the Southeastern Anatolia Project, a plan of many dams and power stations on the Euphrates and Tigris. The aim was to bring electricity, irrigation and jobs to Turkey's poorest region, which is mostly Kurdish. Its power station is one of the largest in the country, and long tunnels carry water from the lake to the dry plain of Harran, where cotton now grows.

The lake drowned villages and ancient sites, among them old Samosata. The dam also gives Turkey control of water that flows on to Syria and Iraq. When the lake began to fill in January 1990, the river was held back for a month, and both countries protested. Water rights on the Euphrates and Tigris remain a source of tension between the three.
sum: A huge rock-fill dam on the Euphrates river in southeastern Turkey, built from 1983 to 1990 and named after Mustafa Kemal Atatürk. It is the largest dam on the river.
